title: Ancillary Credits Counted against a Charge — Resident Funds Returns
content:
In the return of a payer-covered transfer from a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account, the charge's unpaid balance is the charge less the payments naming it and less **the credits counted against it**. Which credits count follows the tier of the resident's open account under Ancillary and Optional Services Billing, because a credit for the coverage of the payer that tier follows records the improper part this return gives back, while a credit for another payer's coverage settled the charge for days that payer covered, like any other credit.

## Credits counted, by ancillary tier

| Ancillary account tier | Credits counted against the charge |
|---|---|
| Ancillary Account, Medicare Part A Consolidated Billing | every credit naming the charge except a credit for a consolidated billing item |
| Ancillary Account, Medical Assistance | every credit naming the charge except a credit for a payer-covered item |
| Ancillary Account, Medicare Part B | every credit naming the charge except a credit for a payer-covered item |
| Ancillary Account, Medicare Advantage | every credit naming the charge except a credit for a payer-covered item |
| Ancillary Account, Hospice Election | every credit naming the charge except a credit for a hospice-related item |
| any other tier | every credit naming the charge |

## Hypothetical illustration

A charge of $143.20 carries $27.50 of payments, a $61.15 credit for a payer-covered item and a $9.40 credit for a price error.

| Tier | Credits counted | Unpaid balance |
|---|---|---|
| Ancillary Account, Medical Assistance | $9.40 | $106.30 |
| Ancillary Account, Medicare Part A Consolidated Billing | $70.55 | $45.15 |
| Ancillary Account, Private Pay | $70.55 | $45.15 |
